content: Trees do not eat their own sweet fruit; rivers do not drink their own waters; the life of the noble is poured out for the welfare of others.
author: Sanskrit Subhashitas
sourceWork: Pibanti nadyah svayameva nambhaha (पिबन्ति नद्यः स्वयमेव नाम्भः) — Subhashita Ratna Bhandagara
explanation: Look at the great banyan tree: it toils through heat and winter to produce nourishing figs, yet takes not a single bite for itself. The majestic Ganges flows thousands of miles without sipping a single drop. Selfish hoarding is contrary to nature; true nobility lives in giving.
practicalInsight: Use your talent, influence, or resources today to uplift someone else's burden with zero expectation of applause.
reflectionPrompt: How much of your daily striving is dedicated exclusively to feeding your own ego versus serving the common good?
